rubrics.justification: The response overstates confidence in grading from a limited single image. The embryo appears poorly visualized/partially collapsed with indistinct ICM and sparse irregular TE, so assigning 3-4BB or 4BC and describing a clearly visible blastocoel and slightly thinned zona is only partly supported and includes likely fabricated detail.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor, sperm parameters, prior cycle history, and endometrium into prognosis reasonably well, though some links are somewhat generic and it assumes favorable endometrial features not provided.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible prognosis framework. Minor issues include overprecision in percentage adjustments and confidence in morphology despite image limitations.

General recommendations such as SET and considering uterine evaluation after repeated failure are aligned, but routine PGT-A at age 33, ERA after only limited failure history, progesterone monitoring/IM supplementation, and stimulation changes are more debatable and not standard guideline-driven recommendations.
The response gives clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, though several suggestions are broader than necessary for this case and some are not strongly evidence-based.
